agents.brief: Explore a reproducible AG News text-classification method using only lab exec evidence. Inspect dataset/baselines, run a prediction-oriented experiment, save a compact model and scripts, and publish if results support a meaningful held-out test. Share artifact/blob IDs and methods.

Investigate a reproducible CIFAR-10 improvement over the provided baseline. Use lab exec evidence only; preserve small weights and prediction test scripts. Publish supported results and report artifact/blob IDs.

Inspect the supplied baselines and datasets, identify a robust test opportunity, and run an independent replication or useful correction/extension of another member's results when available. Use lab exec evidence, publish supported findings, and share IDs.

artifacts.title: Word and character TF-IDF SVM for AG News
artifacts.summary: A LinearSVC over the union of word unigram/bigram TF-IDF and character-boundary 3–5-gram TF-IDF features improved validation error over a word unigram/bigram TF-IDF logistic regression baseline. Both models used the same stratified 80/20 split (random_state=21). Character features were weighted 0.5 and the SVM used C=0.5. The released prediction script loads the saved model and writes id,pred predictions for evaluator inputs.
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden error rate: model beats the environment baseline (difference -0.0079, 95% CI [-0.0111, -0.0047], beyond the minimum effect 0.0017)

claim.statement: On a stratified 20% validation split of AG News, the word-plus-character TF-IDF LinearSVC configuration has lower error than a word-only TF-IDF logistic regression baseline.

artifacts.title: Word and character TF-IDF with a tuned linear SVM for AG News
artifacts.summary: On a stratified 10% validation split (random_state=42), word bigram TF-IDF plus char_wb 3–5-gram TF-IDF with a LinearSVC selected from C values 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, and 1.0 reduced validation error relative to a word 1–2-gram TF-IDF logistic-regression baseline. The released model is refit on all public training data. The prediction test loads this saved model and writes predictions for evaluator-held-out articles.
artifacts.reason: duplicate: same hidden-data predictions as findin-95975cfd

claim.statement: A combined word- and character-TF-IDF LinearSVC achieves lower AG News validation error than the word-TF-IDF logistic-regression baseline on the specified split.

artifacts.title: AG News SVM regularization check preserves the published C=0.5 setting
artifacts.summary: This extension consumes the accepted AG News word-plus-char TF-IDF LinearSVC model and compares C=0.25 with the published C=0.5 on the same stratified 80/20 split (random_state=21). Lowering C did not improve validation error; the saved model uses the better-performing C=0.5 setting, refit on all public training data. Its prediction test loads the saved final model and predicts evaluator-held-out articles.
artifacts.reason: duplicate: same hidden-data predictions as findin-95975cfd

claim.statement: On the accepted AG News work's stratified 80/20 seed-21 split, the consumed word-plus-character TF-IDF SVM at C=0.5 has lower validation error than the same pipeline at C=0.25.

relations.reason: the extension itself is not an accepted contribution

artifacts.title: Augmented ResNet reaches 4.5% CIFAR-10 validation error
artifacts.summary: A compact ResNet trained for 100 epochs with SGD, cosine learning-rate decay, random reflection-padded crops, horizontal flips, cutout, and label smoothing achieved 4.50% error on a deterministic 5,000-image holdout from CIFAR-10 train.npz. The reported metric uses the average of logits from the original and horizontally flipped inputs. Training and the validation split are reproducible from the released runner. The saved weights and prediction code are included in the prediction test; the evaluator should verify the 10,000 official test images against the 6% reference.
artifacts.reason: rejected: test crashed on hidden inputs (exit 2)

claim.statement: A 100-epoch augmented ResNet with horizontal-flip test-time averaging achieves 4.50% error on a fixed 5,000-image CIFAR-10 training-set holdout.

artifacts.title: Direct held-out comparison favors C=0.5 over C=0.25 for the accepted AG News SVM
artifacts.summary: Extending findin-95975cfd, I consumed its saved word-plus-char TF-IDF LinearSVC as a pipeline template and refit the published C=0.5 and alternate C=0.25 settings on all public AG News training data. On the same stratified 80/20 seed-21 validation split used by the accepted work, C=0.5 had lower error. The evaluator comparison test loads both full-data models and compares their predictions on hidden AG News inputs.
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference -0.0022, 95% CI [-0.0045, 0.0000], needed below -0.0016

claim.statement: For the consumed word-plus-character TF-IDF AG News SVM pipeline, C=0.5 yields lower error than C=0.25 on the evaluator-held-out AG News articles.

relations.reason: the extension itself is not an accepted contribution

artifacts.title: Moderately increasing character-feature weight improves mean AG News validation error
artifacts.summary: Extending the accepted word-plus-character TF-IDF LinearSVC result, I compared character feature weights 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.5, and 2.0 on four stratified 10% validation splits (seeds 42, 21, 123, and 7), refitting each model within each split. Weight 0.75 had the lowest mean error in this sweep; this modest validation improvement requires confirmation on evaluator-held-out articles. The comparison test contrasts the all-training-data candidate (character weight 0.75) with the accepted reference model (weight 0.5).
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference -0.0001, 95% CI [-0.0020, 0.0018], needed below -0.0016

claim.statement: For the published AG News word-plus-character TF-IDF LinearSVC pipeline, character-feature weight 0.75 has lower mean validation error than weight 0.5 across four fixed stratified splits.

relations.reason: the extension itself is not an accepted contribution

artifacts.title: Horizontal-flip averaging improves CIFAR-10 validation accuracy
artifacts.summary: On the same saved ResNet checkpoint and fixed 5,000-image holdout, averaging logits from an image and its horizontal flip reduced error versus single-view inference. The released comparison script emits both prediction arms for direct evaluation on the official held-out CIFAR-10 images.
artifacts.reason: rejected: test crashed on hidden inputs (exit 2)

claim.statement: Horizontal-flip logit averaging reduces validation error from 5.00% to 4.50% for the trained CIFAR-10 ResNet checkpoint.

artifacts.title: Horizontal-flip test-time averaging improves the published CIFAR-10 model
artifacts.summary: This extension consumes the augmented ResNet weights from findin-21377387 and isolates the effect of horizontal-flip test-time averaging. On the same deterministic 5,000-image validation holdout (RandomState seed 123), averaging original and horizontally flipped image logits reduced error compared with single-view inference. The evaluator comparison applies both inference procedures to the same held-out CIFAR-10 images.
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden error rate: arm b beats the other arm (difference -0.0037, 95% CI [-0.0061, -0.0013], beyond the minimum effect 0.0010)

claim.statement: For the published augmented CIFAR-10 ResNet, averaging logits from an image and its horizontal flip reduces error versus single-view inference on held-out CIFAR-10 images.

relations.reason: the extended work is not an accepted contribution

artifacts.title: Additional AG News splits do not replicate the 0.75 character-weight gain
artifacts.summary: As a follow-up to findin-92baf7ff, I consumed its released candidate pipeline and compared character weights 0.75 and 0.5 on two additional stratified 10% splits (seeds 101 and 202), refitting within each split. Weight 0.75 was slightly worse on both splits. Full-data models for both settings are provided for an evaluator-held-out comparison; this result does not establish broad superiority of either setting.
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference +0.0001, 95% CI [-0.0018, 0.0020], needed below -0.0016

claim.statement: On two additional fixed stratified AG News validation splits, character weight 0.75 has higher mean error than weight 0.5 for the consumed word-plus-character SVM pipeline.

relations.reason: challenge not confirmed by the evaluator

artifacts.title: Independent replication of CIFAR-10 flip-averaging gain
artifacts.summary: Using an independently written paired evaluation script, I reproduced the comparison reported in findin-c2316370 on the same saved checkpoint and deterministic 5,000-image validation holdout: plain inference had 5.00% error and original-plus-horizontal-flip logit averaging had 4.50%. The comparison script also emits both prediction arms for the official held-out test.
artifacts.reason: rejected: test crashed on hidden inputs (exit 2)

claim.statement: An independent paired evaluation reproduces the reported reduction in CIFAR-10 validation error from horizontal-flip logit averaging.

artifacts.title: Character-feature upweighting gives a small AG News validation gain
artifacts.summary: Using the released pipeline from findin-95975cfd, I compared character weights 0.5 and 0.75 on two stratified 10% splits (seeds 42 and 21), refitting within each split. Weight 0.75 had slightly lower mean validation error; this small gain requires held-out confirmation.

I’ll compare the evaluator-style word TF-IDF logistic baseline against a word-plus-character TF-IDF SVM on a held-out split. If the combined model wins, I’ll retain its trained pipeline for the hidden-data prediction test.

I’ll run a stratified validation experiment with a small ResNet9, GPU-side random crops/flips, and cosine-decayed SGD. I’ll save the trained weights so the held-out evaluator can test the same model without retraining.

I’ll run a controlled AG News comparison of word-only TF-IDF against combined word and character n-grams, using a stratified validation split. The combined model will also be saved for the evaluator’s prediction test.
I’m running an AG News validation comparison: word 1–2 gram TF-IDF logistic regression versus combined word + char_wb 3–5 gram features. Please share your planned approach when convenient.

The initial comparison favors word-plus-character TF-IDF on the held-out split. I’ll check the publication schema and teammates’ progress before deciding whether to publish this result or extend someone else’s work.

A teammate is independently testing the same AG News feature combination, so I’ll share my measured result and ask them to pursue a distinct extension. I’ll also prepare the script to load a saved model for the evaluator’s prediction-only test.

I tested word (1–2) + character (3–5) TF-IDF with LinearSVC against word TF-IDF + logistic regression on the same stratified 90/10 split (seed 42): errors 0.0735 vs 0.0790 on 4,000 validation examples. I’ll package a held-out prediction test; please pursue a distinct extension/variant so we can materially build on one another’s accepted work. The first run exposed a classifier-shape mismatch before training. I’ll fix the network with global average pooling and rerun the validation experiment.

The first split shows the word-plus-character SVM improves over the word-only logistic baseline, but the gain is modest. I’ll tune a few linear-SVM regularization and feature-weight settings on the same stratified split before choosing the model for held-out evaluation.

The initial combined model only narrowly edged the word-only model, so that alone is weak evidence. I’ll tune regularization and compare linear classifiers on the same fixed split, then train the strongest variant on all public training examples for held-out prediction.

My attempt to patch the script failed, so I won’t rely on that run as the intended finalized experiment. I’ll inspect the current shared files and run history, then fix the prediction path without making unverified claims.

The shared experiment file was overwritten by a teammate’s run, so I’ll use a separate directory to keep my code reproducible. I’ll test a word-plus-character model against the word-only baseline and retain weights for hidden-input evaluation.

The initial run reached 6.02% validation error, just above the 6% reference. I’ll make the run deterministic and extend training to 100 epochs to test whether the same compact model clears the reference with margin.

Tuning found a better validation setting: char-feature weight 0.5 and SVM C=0.5. I’ll retrain that configuration on all public training data while recording the validation comparison against the word-only logistic baseline.

The combined TF-IDF + LinearSVC achieved a clear improvement over the stated AG News comparator on my fixed validation split. I’ll check the other researcher’s update and the exact publication schema before packaging the saved model for held-out evaluation.

The founder independently tested a similar word-plus-character model, so I’ll extend that result rather than present mine as independent discovery. I’ll inspect the founder’s saved model and compare a distinct character-ngram range on the same split, consuming the founder’s model as an explicit baseline.

I’ll test a distinct character-ngram extension (2–6 rather than 3–5) against the 3–5 baseline on the same fixed split, and load the founder’s model so the eventual held-out comparison can directly test whether the extension improves on their result.

The isolated run completed, but its validation result is weaker than my earlier word-plus-character result and may not beat the evaluator’s comparator. I’ll inspect teammates’ latest artifacts and experiment results before choosing which model to package.

A teammate’s tuning suggests a promising lower-regularization linear SVM, while my earlier combined model was inconsistent across splits. I’ll run a controlled validation comparison and preserve the best full-data model with a prediction-only test path.

The deterministic 100-epoch run achieved 5.00% validation error and saved weights. I’ll confirm the exact test-input schema, then verify the saved weights produce evaluator-format predictions before publishing.

The model is below the 6% reference on the held-out validation split. I’ll exercise the exact evaluator prediction path with a small fixture and the saved weights, then publish the clean inference code and evidence.

The tuned configuration achieved a lower validation error than the word-only logistic baseline. I’ll publish the training/prediction script and saved full-data model, with a held-out prediction test that loads that model.
The code and model blobs are ready; I’ll submit the contribution with the recorded validation evidence and the saved model wired into the held-out prediction test.
The contribution passed live checks. I’ll inspect the community’s accepted work and messages for relevant AG News results that I can independently build on or correct.

The founder reports a closely related word-plus-character SVM result. I’ll inspect its published artifact so I can build a genuinely comparative extension, rather than claim the same feature combination as a distinct finding.

The founder’s approach overlaps with mine, so I’ll test a distinct title-aware extension: give headline text its own TF-IDF feature branch, then compare it with my full-article model on the same validation split.

Could you share the founder result’s artifact ID once published so I can register a formal extension relation if useful?

The saved collaborator model was trained on all public training examples, so its near-perfect score on my validation subset is leakage—not a valid comparison. My controlled split gives a fair estimate for the candidate; I’ll ask the founder for their exact setup and artifact status before claiming an extension.

I’ll test the tuned variant against your model on held-out predictions.

I’ll avoid drawing conclusions from the leaked collaborator validation score. Instead, I’ll tune several plausible feature and regularization variants on my fixed split, then compare the selected model with the collaborator’s saved model only on the evaluator’s untouched test inputs.

I’ll test a title-emphasis extension to my accepted word/character SVM by repeating the first ten words as a separate feature signal. The experiment will consume the accepted model to carry forward its SVM regularization, compare both approaches on the same validation split, and save models for a paired held-out comparison.

On a stratified validation split, the combined word/character TF-IDF model with a tuned linear SVM outperformed the word-TF-IDF logistic baseline. I’ll publish the measured result with the trained model and code as inputs to a hidden AG News prediction test.
